title: FAQ:
title_q: “Did My Money Actually Do What I Thought It Would?”
title_short: Sonam · FAQ 2 · Did my money do what I thought?
headline: You do not have to take Watsi's word for it: the payments are public, the update comes back to you, and 100% goes to the medical partner, so you can follow the money.
story: Sonam answers one donor question in one clean take: did my money actually do what I thought it would? She says it is a fair question, then shows how Watsi makes the whole process visible.

Three proofs, in her order: the public transparency document (“a very boring Google sheet”), the update that closes the loop, and 100% going straight to the medical partner. She ends on the work before the gift and the line that names the video: you can actually follow the money.
do: Open on the question as text, over the group walking. Then cut straight to her answer.
Cut from the one clean take, Mincho7651. Keep her order.
Show the real transparency document, recorded fresh from watsi.org.
Fresh Clinica Noel B-roll from 20 Oct only.
Captions on the whole time she speaks, one line at a time.
dont: No Smile Train logo or sign in any frame (the pink “Fundación SmileTrain” wall is in Mincho7594).
No reused hospital entrance or patient sequence from the July cuts.
No child's face without a release. Never name the CSC hospital.
No fake website or spreadsheet. Only real pages, recorded fresh.

bp_intro: All bites are from Mincho7651.MP4 (1:42, 4K, 23.976 fps, one locked-off camera, teleprompter). Times are mm:ss.s in that clip, from the word-level transcript (output.json). Word times can drift by about 0.2 s: find each cut on the waveform. The transcript writes Watsi as “Whatsy”: it is Watsi. No frames were pulled yet: shots are named from visual.json, so check each one on scrub.

rows.visual: No face yet. Natural movement: Mincho7629.MP4 00:00.5 to 00:03.5, the Watsi group walking down a Clinica Noel corridor (visual.json: women walking a corridor, numbers on the walls, a pink door). Check on scrub that no Smile Train logo is in frame. Her own read of the question is not used: the text replaces it.
rows.motion: Hook text on frame 1: Did my money actually do what I thought it would? Already on screen at 0:00, does not animate on. Top third, Lato Bold, Watsi yellow #FFCC33, soft shadow, big. It doubles as the thumbnail. Holds to 00:03, then cut straight to Sonam.
rows.sfx: Room tone from the corridor clip, low.
rows.music: Music starts on frame 1. Warm, light, hopeful. No drums, no lyrics.

shots.what: The Watsi group walks down a corridor

rows.visual: Sonam to camera, the full 16:9 frame: seated, orange T-shirt with a logo, the Clinica Noel name on the wall behind her. One take, locked off. Start on “It's”. Face only: this is where we meet her.
rows.motion: Hook text off at 00:03. Name super at 00:04 for 3 s, lower left, above the captions, large: <q>Sonam Singh</q> / Director of Marketing & Insights. Captions on from her first word.

voice.quote: It's a completely reasonable question. If we are asking you to trust us with your money, we should show you what happens to it. That's why we make the whole process pretty unusually visible.

rows.music: Bed 18 to 20 dB under her voice.

rows.visual: Her face on “In addition”. On “monthly reports” cut to Mincho7647.MP4 00:26.5 to 00:30.0: a computer monitor with the Watsi logo at Clinica Noel (visual.json; check on scrub). On “This has a receipt” cut to a screen recording of Watsi's real transparency document, opened from watsi.org. Record it fresh on a laptop, 1920×1080. Never fake a page. Scroll slowly to one row. Back to her face when the row ends.
rows.motion: Brackets on one receipt row in the screen recording, for 3 s, after the scroll stops. Captions on.

voice.quote: In addition to sharing not just annual financial statements on watsi.org but even monthly reports, we also publish payments in real-time transparency document. This has a receipt of each payment we make to our medical partners for each individual patients.

rows.sfx: One soft UI tap on the cut to the screen recording. Nothing else.

shots.what: Monitor with the Watsi logo at Clinica Noel

rows.visual: Her face the whole row. She is funny here (“a boring Google sheet”). The face is the strongest picture, so no cutaway. One slow 3% push-in across the row.
rows.motion: Top text as she says it, about 00:40.4: a very boring Google sheet. Lato Bold, white. Out after 2.5 s. Captions on.

voice.quote: And okay, I'll admit our transparency document is a little old-school but I also love how simple it is. It's just a boring Google sheet but maybe in a world where everything is getting more complicated and more polished, a very boring Google sheet is what becomes rare.

rows.music: Bed steady. Let her joke land, no hit.

rows.visual: Her face on “Okay and then”. On “we send you an update” cut to Mincho7708.MP4 00:08.0 to 00:11.0: a guest in a white cap sits with a young boy, both hold cards, a man takes a photo (visual.json). Then Mincho7713.MP4 00:07.0 to 00:10.0: a family around a table at the art activity, the boy holds a green toy. Back to her face on “and you really hear from them”. Children: use only with a release (ask Nick).

voice.quote: Okay and then we also close the communication loop. Once a patient has had the treatment, we send you an update about what happened to them, how they're doing, what they are back to and you really hear from them.

shots.what: Guest and a boy hold cards
A family at the art activity table

rows.visual: Her face on “And the donation itself”. On “goes directly to the medical partner” cut to Mincho7602.MP4 01:10.0 to 01:13.0: a surgeon in scrubs and a colleague in a blue cap talk in the corridor (visual.json). Then Mincho7603.MP4 00:12.0 to 00:15.0: healthcare workers in scrubs talk in the corridor. Back to her face on “it pays for the surgery you decided to support.” No patient faces.
rows.motion: Number pop <q>100%</q> with the line <q>of it goes directly to the medical partner</q>, top third, on her words, 3 s. Captions on.

voice.quote: And the donation itself, 100% of it goes directly to the medical partner providing the care. It doesn't pass through the patient or their family, it isn't simply given to someone to spend however they want, it pays for the surgery you decided to support.

shots.what: Surgeon and colleague talk in the corridor
Healthcare workers talk in the corridor

rows.visual: Her face on “There's also a lot of work”. On “due diligence” cut to Mincho7632.MP4 00:05.0 to 00:08.0: the group in a meeting room, some standing, some seated (visual.json, likely the welcome with Clinica Noel leadership). On “regularly review” cut to Mincho7644.MP4 00:46.0 to 00:49.0: medical staff seated at a laptop, talking (visual.json). Back to her face for the end of the line.

voice.quote: There's also a lot of work that happens before your donation ever gets there that we could do an even better job talking about. We do initial and ongoing due diligence with our medical partner, stay in close communication with them for any need and challenges that come up and regularly review how each program is operating.

shots.what: The group in a meeting room

rows.visual: Her face. Hold 0.7 s after “money.”, then cut to the end card. No fade.
rows.motion: Top text on her words: <q>you can actually follow the money.</q> Lato Bold, Watsi yellow. Holds to the cut. Captions on.

voice.quote: So basically you don't just have to take our word for it, you can actually follow the money.

rows.visual: Clean end card, full frame. Light cyan #D3EDFA background. Navy is never a background.
rows.motion: watsi.org, all lowercase, Lato, navy #2E2844. One line. Nothing under it. No logo before this card.
rows.music: Music out with a 1 s fade.

−14 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP peak. Music always under the voice.

“100%” is written with the % sign, the same in the caption and the number pop.
